assessment.summary: BRAF is one of the most extensively characterized and druggable oncology targets in the human kinome, with 5 approved small-molecule inhibitors, over 11,000 IC50 measurements in ChEMBL, and 20 high-resolution crystal structures including 18 with bound ligands. The target is strongly validated across multiple cancer indications (melanoma, colorectal, thyroid, lung, and others) driven primarily by the activating V600E mutation. Druggability is unambiguously high across all evidence dimensions.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 66.4 and only 55% high-confidence residues suggest disordered regions (likely N-terminal regulatory and linker segments) not resolved in crystal structures — conformational dynamics of full-length BRAF not fully captured

Resistance mechanisms (e.g., paradoxical ERK activation, BRAF amplification, splice variants, RAS mutations) are well-known but structural/chemical solutions for next-generation inhibitors overcoming all resistance modalities remain incomplete
Limited structural and chemical data for BRAF in the context of its dimeric signaling state and RAS interaction interface, which are relevant for paradox-breaker inhibitor design
Clinical efficacy data for BRAF inhibition in some tumor types (e.g., colorectal cancer as monotherapy) is poor due to feedback reactivation; combination strategies are still being optimized
No explicit allosteric binding site data beyond the ATP-competitive site and known αC-helix/DFG-loop pockets in the available evidence summary
